text:
lisa (People Ops): Quick follow-up from today’s all-hands — putting answers to the promo/comp questions here. Ask anything and we’ll reply or loop in leads.
jamie (People Ops): TL;DR: promos effective 1st of next month, retroactive pay handled same payroll cycle but may show as separate line item.
ryan (IC): Is the promo effective date based on calendar month or the payroll cutoff? I.e., if promotion approved 29th, is it 1st?
maria (Eng Manager): We had a case last cycle where approval came on 30th and HR applied pay from the 1st. Managers: try to finalize approvals by the 25th to avoid payroll edge cases.
toni (Finance): Confirming — effective date is first of next month; payroll cutoff is the 25th, so approvals after 25th still show as effective 1st but may hit retro pay in the following payroll run.
lisa (People Ops): Adding the formal guideline: approvals by 25th => salary change reflected in next payroll as base pay; approvals after 25th => retroactive adjustment in subsequent run.
ryan (IC): How will retro pay appear? I don’t want surprises on my payslip.
toni (Finance): It’ll be a separate adjustment line labeled "Retroactive salary adjustment" with the period covered. Gross amounts will be shown; standard taxes apply.
jamie (People Ops): On promotion letters — managers will receive the template in the manager kit after calibration. Please don’t edit compensation numbers in the template; contact people-ops for exceptions.
maria (Eng Manager): Calibration notes — are we still using the same rubric as last cycle (impact, scope, autonomy)? I have a couple of borderline cases.
multi (promo-bot): Reminder: calibration meeting scheduled Thu 10am PT. Add your calibration docs to the shared drive by Wed 8pm PT.
lisa (People Ops): Yes, same rubric. For borderline cases, include two short examples (one showing current level behavior, one showing target level behavior). That helps committees.
ryan (IC): If my manager says no but I believe I qualify, what’s the appeal?
jamie (People Ops): We encourage first talking with your manager and people partner. If unresolved, file a calibration appeal — template in the promo playbook. Appeals are reviewed by a small cross-functional committee; outcome communicated within 10 business days.
ryan (IC): Cool, thanks.
maria (Eng Manager): Headcount question: if a promotion changes comp band and we need approval for a hire backfill, does that slow approval?
lisa (People Ops): Promotion itself does not block headcount approvals. If comp change increases budget pressure, Finance flags it in the approval flow but we try to separate promotion decisions from backfill timing.
lisa (People Ops): If a promotion moves someone to an "above-band" comp, we’ll include a short note to Finance explaining the rationales — this can speed approvals.
toni (Finance): For above-band comp, expect an additional review step but we aim for <5 business days.
aman (alex (CEO)): Quick note from leadership: promotions and comp are high priority — we’ll continue investing to keep bands competitive. If teams are hitting retention issues, flag us immediately.
ryan (IC): Any change to equity refresh cadence with promos?
jamie (People Ops): No change to the standard refresh cadence this cycle. Equity refreshes are still handled by Talent comp and will be communicated separately.
lisa (People Ops): Benefit question from Slack earlier — open enrollment window dates are unchanged. We’ll send the calendar invite + FAQ doc by EOD. Link to playbook: https://company.share/promo-playbook (manager kit + templates).
maria (Eng Manager): One practical ask — can people-ops provide a short checklist we can paste into 1:1s so managers don’t miss docs?
jamie (People Ops): Yes — we’ll drop a 1:1 checklist snippet into the manager kit by tomorrow. Example snippet:
```
1) Confirm examples of impact (2 bullets)
2) Review calibration rubric
3) Confirm compensation band mapping
4) Submit approval by 25th
```
ryan (IC): Appreciate that. Last Q: will promotion announcements go to company slack or team-only?
lisa (People Ops): Standard is team-first (manager-driven), then we send a people-ops templated announcement to #general. If manager prefers, we can hold company announcement for special cases.
maria (Eng Manager): Thanks — this clarifies a ton.
lisa (People Ops): Thanks everyone — we’ll keep this thread updated as questions come in. If you need something private, DM people-ops or open a ticket at https://company.help/pplops.
